title: When Water Systems Are Attacked, Children Pay the Highest Price
title_zh: 供水系统遇袭时，儿童付出最高代价
source_name: UN News — “Children at risk as war zone attacks on water and sanitation more than triple” (5 Nov 2026); UNICEF Water Under Fire 4 report
summary_zh: 联合国儿童基金会 11 月 5 日发布《战火中的水》第四期报告：2021 至 2025 年间，冲突地区针对供水与环卫系统的袭击增加了两倍以上，从 8 国不足 45 起升至 15 国逾 135 起。袭击包括轰炸水厂管道、污染水源、限制净水药剂，也会因断电间接停水。儿童因此更易生病、营养不良、失学，取水时还可能遭受暴力。儿基会强调：修修补补不能代替国际人道法要求的保护，且相关人道资金目前只到位约 26%。
paragraphs: Attacks that damaged or destroyed water and sanitation systems in conflict zones more than tripled between 2021 and 2025, according to a new UNICEF report released on 5 November. The rise increases children's risk of disease outbreaks, malnutrition and violence when they try to obtain safe water.

The latest Water Under Fire study covers January 2021 to June 2026 and documents assaults on water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) systems — and on the people who run and rely on them — in 23 countries and territories. Recorded incidents climbed from fewer than 45 across eight countries in 2021 to more than 135 across 15 countries in 2025.

The report lists seven types of assault. They range from strikes on treatment plants, pipelines and wells to the contamination of water sources and restrictions on spare parts and chemicals needed to treat water. In Sudan, by March 2024 only one of 13 water treatment plants in Khartoum state was fully working. In the Gaza Strip, more than 130,000 metres of sewage pipelines have been destroyed since October 2023.

Disruptions can also happen when pipes and pumps look fine. In Iraq, a drone attack on a gas field in November 2025 cut electricity production in the Kurdistan region by about 80 per cent, forcing authorities to ration power between water projects, hospitals and cities. Without electricity, pumping stations stop, and a power cut quickly becomes a water crisis.

UNICEF calls these knock-on harms "reverberating effects". Health centres cannot sterilize equipment, deliver babies safely or prepare therapeutic milk for severely malnourished children. Women and girls, who often fetch water for their families, face sexual violence and lost school time. Children have been killed or injured while waiting in line for water, and 14 water facility workers were recorded killed in Lebanon during the 2024 conflict.

Across countries with a coordinated WASH response, 137.9 million people need help, yet only 26 per cent of the required funding has arrived this year. "Repairs cannot substitute for the protection of these facilities that is required under international humanitarian law," said UNICEF Executive Director Catherine Russell. The agency urges warring parties and donors to protect water systems, collect better data on attacks, keep humanitarian workers safe, and invest in services that can survive conflict.
paragraphs_zh: 联合国儿童基金会 11 月 5 日发布的新报告显示，2021 至 2025 年间，冲突地区损坏或摧毁供水与环卫系统的袭击增加了两倍以上。这一上升使儿童在设法获取安全用水时，更容易面临疾病暴发、营养不良和暴力风险。
最新一期《战火中的水》研究报告覆盖 2021 年 1 月至 2026 年 6 月，记录了 23 个国家和地区针对供水、环卫与卫生（WASH）系统——以及运行和依赖这些设施的人——的袭击。有记录的事件从 2021 年 8 个国家不足 45 起，上升到 2025 年 15 个国家逾 135 起。
报告列出七类袭击方式，从打击水厂、管道和水井，到污染水源，再到限制净水所需的备件和化学品。在苏丹，到 2024 年 3 月，喀土穆州 13 座水处理厂中只有一座完全运转。在加沙地带，自 2023 年 10 月以来，已有超过 13 万米污水管道被毁。
即便管道和水泵看似完好，供水也可能中断。在伊拉克，2025 年 11 月一次针对气田的无人机袭击使库尔德地区发电量大约减少 80%，当局不得不在供水项目、医院和城市之间分配电力。没有电，泵站就会停转，停电很快就会变成水危机。
儿基会把这些连锁伤害称为“回响效应”。卫生机构无法消毒器械、安全接生，也无法为严重营养不良的儿童配制治疗奶。常常为家人取水的妇女和女童面临性暴力和失学风险。儿童在排队等水时曾被打死或打伤；2024 年冲突期间，黎巴嫩有记录显示 14 名供水设施工作人员遇害。
在开展协调一致的 WASH 人道响应的国家中，有 1.379 亿人需要援助，但今年所需资金仅到位 26%。儿基会执行主任凯瑟琳·拉塞尔说：“修修补补不能代替国际人道法所要求的对这些设施的保护。”该机构敦促交战各方与捐助方保护供水系统、更好地收集袭击数据、保障人道工作者安全，并投资建设能在冲突中继续运转的服务。

questions.prompt: What is the main point of the passage?
options: UNICEF has already solved most water problems in conflict zones.
Attacks on water and sanitation systems in war zones have risen sharply, harming children, and protection matters more than repairs alone.
Most water shortages today are caused by natural droughts, not conflict.
Electricity systems are never linked to water supply.
questions.explanation: 主旨：冲突地区针对供水与环卫系统的袭击大幅增加，儿童受害最重；儿基会强调保护这些设施比单纯修修补补更重要。

evidence.quote: Attacks that damaged or destroyed water and sanitation systems in conflict zones more than tripled between 2021 and 2025

questions.prompt: How many recorded WASH-related attack incidents were there across 15 countries in 2025?

evidence.quote: Recorded incidents climbed from fewer than 45 across eight countries in 2021 to more than 135 across 15 countries in 2025.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred from Catherine Russell's comment about repairs?
options: Fixing damaged pipes is enough if funding arrives quickly.
UNICEF believes legal protection of water facilities is essential and cannot be replaced by patching them up after attacks.
International humanitarian law does not cover water systems.
Donors should stop funding water repairs altogether.
questions.explanation: 拉塞尔说“修修补补不能代替国际人道法要求的保护”，可推断儿基会认为法律上的保护不可或缺，事后修补无法取代事先保护。
